## About

My work combines **statistical reasoning, machine learning, causal inference, and production data systems**. I have developed machine-learning models for **customer churn and reactivation** for one of Brazil's largest football clubs, conducted applied econometric research at **UCLA**, and contributed to a **World Bank** research project.

I have also designed and migrated **production-grade data pipelines and analytics platforms** using **Python, SQL, dbt, Snowflake, Databricks, and AWS**, working across industries and developing experience in building reliable, scalable data systems.

Building on this interdisciplinary background, I am increasingly interested in **AI systems development, evaluation, and governance**, including **LLM-based applications, RAG, and AI agents**. Through [**AI Governance Lab**](https://aigovernancelab.org/), I am exploring how **AI systems, empirical evidence, and causal reasoning** can support better institutional decision-making, responsible AI adoption, and public policy.

## Quantitative Methods & Applied Research {#selected-projects}

My background includes **statistics, econometrics, applied data science, and quantitative research**, with previous projects exploring **causal inference** and **program evaluation**. I remain interested in applying these foundations to **AI evaluation, governance, and public policy**.

### Causal Inference Projects

- [**Customer-Satisfaction Program**](https://github.com/caiocvelasco/project07-venv-causal-inference-difference-in-differences-program-evaluation.git): Examining the impact of a customer-satisfaction initiative with **Difference-in-Differences**.
- [**Recommendation System Impact**](https://github.com/caiocvelasco/project08-venv-causal-inference-propensity-score-difference-in-differences-program-evaluation.git): Assessing a recommendation system with **Propensity Score Matching and Difference-in-Differences**.
